This question has been on my mind for quite a while now. If you look back in the 50s, 60s , 70s, 80s, and 90s, you can name bands that have had enormous impacts on music. I've been thinking about what artists will be remembered as influential decades from now,. So, in other words, in 30-50 years, what artist will we remember as starting a new movement, genre, style, etc?
Who do you think is the most recent artist that has had a major influence?

I'd have to go with Meshuggah (suprise, suprise, from the creator of /v/djent). People not in touch with the metal scene are probably unaware of them, but despite their lack of popularity, they did have a large impact on metal. When I thought of this question, all I could think of were artists that had large influences on their respective genres, and Meshuggah seems to take the cake on that one. Djent (the style of metal they are credited for creating) is very recent in the metal scene, and so it makes sense to say their influence is recent, despite starting in the 90s.

I think J. Cole and Kendrick Lamar have some serious potential to change a lot of general misconceptions of what rap and hip hop are about.

On the flip, I think Lil Wayne was pretty influential to extending the arms of hip hop and rap into a mainstream that we all know/love/hate today.

I just think of where he started and where/what's he's found influence in and it's pretty clear.

And on the flip of flip again we now have Taylor Swift and K. Lamar working doing songs too. I'm not saying this is because of Weezy but I'm just sayin' I think a reason why this doesn't seem so far fetched is because of his influence in pop and other genres.
The Strokes! I think they could have become the biggest group in the world.

After Is This It and Room on Fire they could have been. Then they started doing what the labels wanted them to do. Then Julian Casablancas became a huge asshole and couldn't be in the same room as his cohorts. Their first two albums (and even some of First Impressions of Earth) could have led them to be a band talked about in 100 years. But they funked up, in my opinion.
Exactly, i used to love their Garage Rock style but i can't stand their new New Wave/Synthpop style.

No one can deny the influence Radiohead has had on the indie music scene. As much as people love to hate on them, it's kind of unfounded. They've been consistently making great records for 20 years. That's a long time to have a very dedicated, very LARGE following. The internationally know hit, Creep, was on their first record. They were the first band of their caliber to release a "free" or "pay what you want" record, In Rainbows. 80% (or so, I don't remember the exact stat) of the people that downloaded that album directly from them paid for that album. Their sounds are innovative, catchy, dark, and any selectoon of songs can relate to almost any alive generation.

With all that said, TKOL was an overall disappointing record...for Radiohead. Which means it was still good.

With THAT said, I did not care for Thom Yorkes latest release, Tomorrow's Modern Boxes. The lack of organic instruments really upset me.

Anyway. End Radiohead rant.
Agree with Radiohead. I think OK Computer will be heralded similarly to how Dark Side of the Moon currently is (if it isn't already).
